governance.note: Inherits the caiso-29 ctfloor-localra lever set (CAMPD net-load-filtered outage windows, EIA-860 cogen-flagged BTM CHP host steam in btm.parquet, F923 per-plant delivered gas + measured monthly hub-spot overlay, measured EIA-930 priced interchange / per-hub intertie / gas-coupled DSW tranches, measured EIA-930 monthly hydro budget, RA must-offer midday gas floor at the measured EIA-930 NG:NG profile, Argus coal-cogen BTM steam-following holdout, CT_PEAKER temperature hot-limb reliability floor). One new lever, tracing to a measured physical input: the CT_PEAKER reliability floor gains a YEAR-ROUND local-RA BASELINE (caiso_ct_floor_base=0.049), the measured median CAMPD CT_PEAKER evening (15-22 local) capacity factor on cool days (TMAX<25 degC), pooled 2023-2025 (scripts/derive_caiso_ct_reliability_floor.py). This is the regression INTERCEPT the existing temperature hot-limb fit clips to zero: frac = clip(base + slope*(TMAX-T0), base, cap). CAISO's Local Capacity Requirement is a year-round load-pocket floor (must-offer minimum holds on mild days, not only at summer peak), which an energy-only LP never picks up. The baseline is a measured CF (forward-derivable and condition-responsive on the same TMAX series as the hot limb), NOT a fit to a TWh residual: it is fixed by the cool-day CF statistic, applied to current available capacity, with the LP dispatching economically above it; no unit is pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no adder/haircut/sigmoid is tuned to the price or volume gap.
governance.improvement_note: Strict improvement over the prior keeper caiso-29 on the two C1-failing classes, both complete-vintage years, with no regression elsewhere: CC_REGULAR +2.33/+3.44 (was +2.87/+3.72), CT_PEAKER -2.47/-2.28 (was -3.37/-3.13); CT_PEAKER 2024 now only 0.10 TWh outside the +-2.18 band. C3 price level unchanged (mean LMP +69.1/+47.1/+52.2% vs +70.0/+47.6/+52.9%) and C2/C5 unchanged. Determination stays NOT-YET: C1 (gas merit split) is a HARD gate the year-round CT baseline narrows but does not close (CC_REGULAR still over, CT_PEAKER still marginally under), and the C3 LMP/scarcity misses are pre-existing. The remaining C1 closure requires netting the CHP/EOR steam-following gas out of the midday RA gas-commitment-floor target so re-pricing the EOR cogens power-only no longer forces CC_REGULAR to backfill them (the gas-floor/CHP coupling, documented in docs/caiso-ct-reliability-floor-2026-06.md).
